newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka army casualties mount in rebel attack.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka army casualties mount in rebel attack.

text.p: Tamil Tiger guerrillas attacked a key northern Sri Lanka army-held town on Thursday but were repulsed after suffering some 500 dead or wounded, Defence Ministry and military officials said.
The fighting raged for most of the day after a pre-dawn rebel raid on Paranthan, a Defence Ministry statement said.
It said 500 rebels were killed or wounded.
"Troops have recovered the bodies of 60 soldiers who died in the attack," military spokesman Brigadier Tissa Jayatunga told Reuters. "We're still searching for more casualties."
The ministry earlier said nine government soldiers were killed and 232 wounded. "The figure of our own troops killed in action is likely to increase," it added.
A London-based spokesmen for the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) denied the army statement of 500 rebel casualties.
"The government claim is totally false," LTTE spokesman Anton Raja said by telephone. "It routinely exaggerates the LTTE deaths to maintain flagging morale among supporters and troops."
Raja said he had no details of the battle.
The military said it rushed aircraft and troop reinforcements to repel the attack on Paranthan, on the mainland just south of the Jaffna peninsula, military officials said.

"The Tigers overran part of our FDL (forward defended locality)," a military official told Reuters. "Two gun positions came under very heavy attack and the guns were destroyed by our troops to prevent them from falling into enemy hands."
Jayatunga said soldiers destroyed several guns to prevent them falling into rebel hands but declined to say how many.
The Defence Ministry said troops had repulsed the raid and that the LTTE guerrillas were withdrawing.
Defence analysts said the Tigers had been trying for a long time to acquire long-range artillery in their effort to tip the military balance.
Last July, the rebels overran the northeastern Mullaitivu army base, killing or capturing more than 1,000 soldiers and dealing the army its biggest blow in the 14-year war.

Two 120 mm artillery pieces and two 120 mm mortars captured in the Mullaitivu raid were believed to have been used in Thursday's fighting, the heaviest since the battle for the town of Kilinochchi last September, military officials said.

The Tigers used human-wave tactics and suicide bombers to overrun defences at Paranthan, a junction town 280 km (185 miles) north of the capital Colombo, in the new year's first major battle, military officials said.

The ministry said troops from the nearby Elephant Pass base, about nine km (six miles) to the north on the neck of the Jaffna peninsula, linked up with the defenders of Paranthan around 3.30 p.m. (0930 GMT).
Bodies of soldiers and rebels were seen in several places as army reinforcements, backed by air force helicopter gunships, were assessing battle damage, other military officials said.
Paranthan sits astride the main north-south highway from Colombo to Jaffna and controls the road junction connecting to the rebel-held northeastern town of Mullaitivu.
Government forces, which captured Paranthan from the rebels last July, pushed further into LTTE territory and took control of Kilinochchi in August, the last major town controlled by the rebels.

The LTTE, which is fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in this predominantly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island, were driven out of their Jaffna peninsula stronghold by government forces in April last year.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war. The LTTE says the toll is much higher.
